## Constitution Check
## Design decisions
## Found and left
## Knobs this plan takes (the record could not settle them)
## Project Structure
## Risks
## Summary
## Technical Context
## The 451 parts this feature takes over
## The phases - each usable on its own
## What retires (451 T302 part 4) and when
### D1 - the lane's tree: the existing landing worktree, adopted into the pool as the lane's reserved tree
### D10 - FR-001's gate-write guard and 451 T405's tree check, by construction plus a fixture
### D11 - what retires, and when (451 T302 parts 1 and 4)
### D12 - the measurement (FR-006, FR-007, FR-010)
### D13 - the coordinator's own commits go out before a builder builds on them
### D14 - done refs, successors and repairs
### D15 - where the code lives
### D2 - what drives the lane: a detached runner of our own, `l7r-gate lane --work`
### D3 - the hand-in's "rebase": the builder's diff applied onto `origin/main` with the carry's rules, then the first pass, then the commit
### D4 - the first pass at hand-in: what a builder can answer is asked; what is the lane's is not
### D5 - when the lane starts a batch, and what it holds (FR-004, 451 T415)
### D6 - a red batch: attribute, else halve; eject; land the rest (US4)
### D7 - the repair: a queue entry a fresh builder takes (US4, US5)
### D8 - the lane's states and its log
### D9 - the coordinator's wake-up: one background command, one status line a batch (FR-005)
preamble

decisions.summary: An ejected change or a carry conflict becomes a repair entry in the queue that a fresh builder takes, not an agent the lane launches.
decisions.why: The GM-approved sketch item 1 says it outright: 'the ejected task returns to the queue as a repair entry'. Item 3 has the coordinator as the dispatcher ('I'd dispatch'), and a builder the coordinator dispatches for the entry is a fresh agent that is neither standing nor the coordinator. The coordinator's context gets one queue line. Nothing asked for is narrowed.

decisions.id: XVI-a / D9 + Risks (judgment wakes with no fresh agent)
decisions.summary: Besides repair entries, the lane wakes the coordinator for a set red twice / arbiter owed (D6 step 4), the push failing twice after a re-run (Risks), and the runner dying (D9). The plan does not say who does the integration work after the wake.
decisions.why: Sketch item 3: 'The only integration work left to me would be the rare case that needs judgment, and there a fresh agent per batch beats me doing it'; the plan's own quote of US5 is 'never a standing integrator, never the coordinator's context'. D7 is presented as the plan's answer to US5, but it covers only ejected changes and carry conflicts. A batch that is green but cannot push twice, and a set the arbiter is asked about, wake the coordinator, and the plan names no fresh agent for that batch, which by default leaves the work in the coordinator's turns. That is exactly the case the GM gave to a fresh agent. No impossibility is claimed and none exists, since D7's repair entry could carry them. (A dead runner needs only `make lane-start`, which is a dispatch, not integration, and is fine.)

decisions.summary: Inside the lane, the red-gate tripwire does not fire on consecutive reds that are steps of one halving.
decisions.why: Applied literally, the tripwire would stop the lane at the second step of any bisection. That defeats the GM-approved sketch item 1 ('On a red result it bisects and ejects the failing change') and FR-004, and the plan says so concretely. Exempting a halving's own steps is legitimate.

decisions.id: XVI-b / D6 step 4, part 2 (everything else the set key exempts)
decisions.summary: The exemption is implemented by keying the tripwire to 'a second red of the SAME sorted set of short shas'. That exempts every lane red, not only a halving's steps.
decisions.why: Judged by its purpose, the key leaves the tripwire unable to fire. Every path the plan names gives a fresh set. Halving runs strictly smaller subsets. After an attributed ejection 'the rest runs again' as a new set. The last survivor is 'ejected without a run of its own'. A repair's hand-in supersedes with a NEW sha (D7, D14), so a task that goes red, is repaired, and goes red again never matches. The Risks re-run follows a GREEN gate, so it can give at most one red. Phase 2 states the result itself: the tripwire by change set 'never sees one set twice'. Phase 3's Verify line ('fires on a second red of one set') tests a state the lane never produces. The tripwire is one of the existing `make land` checks (D4 lists it among the first pass's checks) that FR-003 says the lane runs and FR-008 says is not dropped. This exception is plausible at the level of wording but empties the check. Required: inside the lane it must still be able to fire on repeated red on the same work, for example a repair's hand-in red again, or one task ejected twice, while staying quiet on a halving's own steps. The plan says how and tests a path that the lane can actually reach.

decisions.id: XVI-c / D3 (rebase as a no-commit apply)
decisions.summary: FR-002's 'rebases onto current main' is done as the builder's diff applied onto origin/main with carry.rs's merge rules (cherry-pick -n) and then committed, because the project forbids git rebase.
decisions.why: The request's purpose ('Conflicts and bookkeeping refusals then get fixed by the builder that has the context, in its own tree') is met in full. The work ends on current main, conflicts stop in the builder's tree for the builder to resolve, and then the first pass and the commit follow in FR-002's order. The only thing lost is the builder's intermediate commits, which nothing asks for. This is a mechanism, not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: In phase 1 the hand-in applies onto the clone's HEAD rather than origin/main; from phase 2 onto origin/main.
decisions.why: In phase 1 the coordinator still lands from its clone, so the clone's HEAD is the main that the work lands on. Applying onto origin/main would put the work on a base without the staged work it was handed out on, which defeats the stated purpose of a hand-in that 'arrives on what it lands on'. From phase 2 the literal origin/main holds. This is a purpose-level justification and is temporary.

decisions.summary: The hand-in asks the first-pass checks a builder can answer and leaves writer_refusal, the mark's hold, the tripwire, claims-in-flight and the gate stamp rows to the lane, which asks them again when it lands.
decisions.why: FR-002 says 'the landing's cheap first pass'. The left-out checks either cannot be answered before a gate (the stamp rows are physically impossible), concern another writer or the ordering of other tasks, or refuse for reasons no builder can cure. Asking them in a builder's tree would defeat the sketch's purpose of having builders fix what they have the context to fix. All of them are still asked at landing, so FR-008 holds. No coverage runs, as FR-002 requires.

decisions.summary: LANE_MAX=6 and LANE_WAIT_S=0 are seeded from the two-tier ceiling and the trial's 'stronger version', because trial 458 has no finding yet; its verdict resets both.
decisions.why: FR-004 seeds the knob from trial 458's finding, and that finding does not exist yet, so seeding from it is impossible today. The GM told the session to start now. The plan labels both values GUESS and commits to resetting them from the trial's verdict.

decisions.id: D5 batch membership vs FR-003 'in order'
decisions.summary: A batch takes every waiting hand-in of the OLDEST hand-in's feature, so a later hand-in of that feature goes ahead of an earlier hand-in of another feature.
decisions.why: FR-003 says the lane 'takes hand-ins from the done refs in order', and D5 itself reads that as hand-in order ('oldest first'). The reason given, that `make land` takes one F=, does not require a reorder. A batch made of the oldest hand-in plus the CONSECUTIVE same-feature hand-ins after it keeps one F= and keeps the order. The reorder buys larger batches, which is a design preference and not one of the grounds for an exception. Required: keep hand-in order, or state the departure as an exception to FR-003 that is ruled on.

decisions.summary: Until phase 3, a red that the gate's record cannot place ejects the whole batch as one repair entry instead of halving.
decisions.why: This is rollout order, not a narrowing of the finished feature: phase 3 in this same plan replaces it with the halving and 'land the rest'. Under XV a phase-3 stall would leave it standing, so FR-004 is met only once phase 3 lands, and the feature is not done until then. Its one entry covers the whole batch, so it is also a fresh agent per batch.

decisions.id: D12 LIKE-window test omits machine load
decisions.summary: A window is LIKE when it holds 8 or more hours of builder work and its time-weighted trees held is within 0.5 of the night's; the machine's load is read but is not part of the test.
decisions.why: FR-010 defines a LIKE window as one whose 'concurrency is close ...: trees held, time-weighted ..., and the machine's load'. The load is one of the two named components, and it is the GM's seventh-message concern ('how much was happening at the time') on a shared container. D12 drops it from the likeness test without saying so, and phase 5 picks 'the first like window' by that test. A window of three trees under very different load would count as like. No justification is given, and the load median is already available (`make sampler-report`). Required: the likeness test includes a load band (a GUESS), and where load differs, both loads are stated beside the figure. Phase 5 already states each figure with its concurrency, so this finding is confined to the likeness test.

decisions.summary: The lane runs in the existing <clone>-land worktree, adopted into the pool under a reserved holder outside the cap.
decisions.why: The spec leaves the tree to the plan. FR-003's 'its own worktree' is met.

decisions.summary: The lane is a detached `l7r-gate lane --work` runner under flock, using the project's runner pattern; the Workflow tool and the Refinery were priced and not taken whole.
decisions.why: The sketch says 'run as a script in its own worktree rather than in my turns'. FR-009's reuse question is answered and recorded (R1).

decisions.summary: Each attempt gets its own file; attribution comes from the gate's Phase lines; halving lands as it goes and ejects the last survivor without a run of its own; there is no flake retry.
decisions.why: This is FR-004 and the sketch's 'bisects and ejects the failing change. The rest of the batch lands'. Nothing pushes ungated (FR-008).

decisions.summary: Repair entries live in the common git dir; the queue serves repairs first (LANE_REPAIR_FIRST).
decisions.why: The entries stay out of the coordinator's tree (FR-001), and the knob is labeled.

decisions.summary: States are computed from refs and an append-only lane log; 'carried' is read against origin/main.
decisions.why: This is internal mechanism and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: The wake-up is `make lane-wait` in the background, one status line per batch; a Stop-guard rule refuses the main session's stop while lane work waits and no lane-wait runs; the prompt hook prints unread lines.
decisions.why: FR-005's wake-up. The Stop rule's reach is only what makes FR-005's wake happen, which is enforcement of the request.

decisions.id: D10 guard fixture, T405 option C
decisions.summary: FR-001 holds because gates run only in the lane tree, pinned by a fixture over two trees; T405 closes by its option (C).
decisions.why: This enforces FR-001.

decisions.summary: After a like window of lane landings, `make land` outside the lane tree is refused (LAND_HERE_OK escape) and land-alone steps 1-6 retire; step 7 moves to take-tip.sh; writers.rs stays.
decisions.why: The refusal enforces FR-001 and makes the lane the one route. Keeping writers.rs honors FR-008.

decisions.summary: One measurement script over both windows: tokens by actor as window totals, task size beside each figure, concurrency stated with each figure, the before figure taken in phase 0.
decisions.why: This is FR-006, FR-007 and FR-010 apart from the likeness test ruled above. Fresh integration agents are left out of the actor list because D7 makes them repair builders, and FR-006 still counts them.

decisions.id: D13 handout refused on unpushed clone commits
decisions.summary: A handout is refused while the clone holds commits that origin/main lacks; the coordinator pushes spec-only filings DIRECT.
decisions.why: This is required by D3's base, and it honors US1's 'nothing it writes waits on a gate' with the existing DIRECT route. The moved coverage premise is measured, not built around.

decisions.summary: A successor or repair handout applies the earlier done commit uncommitted and supersedes its ref; it waits only on an open batch.
decisions.why: Internal mechanism that serves the sketch.

decisions.summary: One new crate; phases 0-5; the knob table.
decisions.why: No decision here narrows the request.

decisions.summary: The lane's tree is the existing <clone>-land worktree, adopted into the pool under a reserved holder outside the cap; knob L7R_LANE_TREE.
decisions.why: FR-003 asks for a worktree of its own and the spec leaves which one to the plan; choosing an existing tree with a warm cache is a design choice inside that.

decisions.summary: 451 T525 (remove the -land worktree when land-alone retires, so the sweep takes its cache) is replaced, not taken over: the worktree stays as the lane's tree and phase 4 closes T525 in 451 with a pointer.
decisions.why: Ruled on D1's own account of T525, since T525's line is not in the bundle and the repository was not read. On that account T525's premise is a DEAD tree once land-alone retires; under this feature the tree is live (the lane gates in it), so the trigger T525 waits on never arises and nothing of 461's request or spec is narrowed. Leaving T525 open would have a later task delete the lane's tree, which would defeat FR-003; closing it with a pointer is the consistent act. The disk question T525 served is not dropped: D11 measures whether the clone's own 104 GB target directory can go once no gate builds there.

decisions.why: US3 asks for tooling, not coordinator turns; FR-009's reuse record is carried by the priced alternatives.

decisions.summary: FR-002's 'rebases' read as applying the builder's diff onto origin/main with the carry's rules in a no-commit form (XVI reading c).
decisions.why: Unchanged since round 1. The project forbids git rebase (no history rewritten), so the literal command is unavailable; the reading keeps FR-002's purpose (the work checked on current main before commit, conflicts answered by the builder) and its order (rebase, first pass, commit).

decisions.summary: HAND_IN_BASE = clone in phase 1, origin from phase 2.
decisions.why: Unchanged since round 1. In phase 1 landings still go through the clone's HEAD, so 'current main' for what a hand-in lands on is the clone's HEAD; applying onto origin/main then would build on a base lacking staged work and defeat FR-002's purpose. Phase 2 onward is the literal ask.

decisions.summary: The hand-in's first pass asks what a builder can answer and leaves to the lane what is the lane's (writer_refusal, the mark's hold, the tripwire, a claims round in flight, gate stamp rows); no coverage.
decisions.why: Unchanged since round 1. FR-002 asks for 'the landing's cheap first pass'; the rows left out are physically meaningless in a builder's own tree (another writer, another task's ordering, a process stop, rows needing the gate), and every one is still asked when the lane lands (FR-008). 'It runs no coverage' is FR-002's own words.

decisions.summary: A batch is the oldest waiting hand-in plus the waiting same-feature hand-ins straight after it in hand-in order, cut at another feature's hand-in, at one D14 holds, or at LANE_MAX = 6; no hand-in pulled ahead of an older one; LANE_WAIT_S = 0.
decisions.why: Round 1 item 3 met: the batch now honors FR-003's 'in order' literally. The knobs are FR-004's own knob, seeded and labeled GUESS because trial 458 has no finding yet.

decisions.summary: Attribution from the gate's own record first, halving only where it names none (or over the several candidates it names), green halves pushed at once, the last survivor ejected; no flake retry.
decisions.why: US4 and FR-004 literally ('first by the gate's own report ... by bisection only where that names none'); the table shows the ceil(log2 n)+1 bound.

decisions.summary: Inside the lane the red-gate tripwire is keyed by TASK: a red counts only when the lane pins a task (ejected red, left last, ejected with an unplaced whole batch); it fires on a task's second pin, stops the batch, files no second repair and runs make arbiter-ask; halving reds pin nobody.
decisions.why: Round 1 item 1's rule is met by the rule as stated: repeated reds on the same work fire (a repair's hand-in red again; one task ejected twice), and the only reds left quiet are a halving's own steps, which by construction are red runs in a row on shrinking subsets. The literal tripwire would stop the lane at the second step of every halving and so defeat US4's bisection. Phase 2's and phase 3's Verify lines now reach both the firing case and the quiet case. One wording gap to close in the same edit as the next decision (not blocking on its own): the table's one-change red runs ('[C] red: C ejected', '[E] red') are none of step 4's three pin kinds as named, and 'a red half pins on nobody' could be read to cover them; step 4 should state that a change ejected after its own one-change red run is pinned (why red), else its repair red again pins only once and the tripwire never fires.

decisions.summary: second_red_gate stands down for any make land run 'carrying' L7R_LANE_BATCH, leaving it to the lane's rule, which reads only eject lines in lane.jsonl.
decisions.why: Nothing binds the stand-down to the lane: not the lane's tree, not the runner's lock, not an open batch in lane.jsonl with that id. A make land in the coordinator's clone with the variable set by hand (the clone route stays until phase 4, and after it under LAND_HERE_OK) has no eject lines, so the lane's rule never sees it and second_red_gate is silent on every red: an unrecorded escape from an existing check, against FR-008 ('nothing of the existing checks is dropped') and against round 1's own requirement that the tripwire be quiet ONLY on a halving's steps. The plan itself priced and rejected an ARBITER_OK on every lane run because 'an escape on every run teaches every run to escape'; an env var nobody records is that escape without the record. Fix: the stand-down applies only to a run in the lane's tree whose L7R_LANE_BATCH names a batch open in lane.jsonl (or a run started by the runner holding lane.lock); any other run, the variable set or not, meets second_red_gate as today; with a red-first fixture that a by-hand make land carrying the variable outside the lane is still stopped on its second red.

decisions.summary: Phase 2 ejects the whole batch as one repair entry for a red the record cannot place; phase 3's halving replaces it.
decisions.why: An interim step of a phased delivery that ends with FR-004 in full in phase 3; each task still takes a pin, so the tripwire is live from phase 2.

decisions.summary: An ejected change becomes a repair entry in a common-dir file that the queue reads first, taken by a fresh builder; every wake whose work is integration (repair, push failed twice as an integrate entry, arbiter owed, carry conflict) goes to a fresh agent the coordinator dispatches; the coordinator's act is one dispatch or command (XVI reading a).
decisions.why: Round 1 item 2 met: D7's table, the Risks entry and D9 now route every integration wake (the push failed twice included, the arbiter's ruling turned into a repair entry) to a fresh builder or the round arbiter, never to the coordinator's own turns. Routing US5's 'fresh agent dispatched for that batch' through the coordinator's dispatch rather than a lane-launched headless agent keeps the agent guards and token booking in force; the agent is still fresh and per batch, so US5's purpose holds.

decisions.summary: Lane states computed from refs and an append-only log; attempt files never overwritten; done refs deleted after push; carried asked against origin/main.
decisions.why: Serves US3/US4's observability and fixes the night's overwritten log.

decisions.summary: make lane-wait as a background command wakes the coordinator once per landed batch and for US5's cases; a Stop rule keeps it armed; the prompt hook prints unread lines; no ceiling.
decisions.why: FR-005 literally. The knobs footer states the Stop rule's trigger differently from D9's body (an unread owed line vs a waiting hand-in or open batch with no lane-wait running); that line is unchanged since round 1 and is an aside, not a finding.

decisions.summary: FR-001 holds by where gates run, pinned by a two-tree fixture; 451 T405 closed by its option (C).
decisions.why: FR-001 and its takeover of 451 T307 part 1.

decisions.summary: Phase 4 refuses make land outside the lane tree (LAND_HERE_OK recorded escape), retires alone.rs and land-alone.sh steps 1-6, keeps writers.rs and step 7 as take-tip.sh; the clone's target dir dropped only once measured unused.
decisions.why: Enforces FR-003's one route and the takeover of 451 T302 parts 1 and 4; FR-008 kept by keeping writers.rs.

decisions.summary: One measurement script over both windows; a LIKE window is 8 h or more of builder work, trees held within 0.5 of the night's AND median load within 0.75-1.25 times the night's; both trees held and both median loads stated beside each figure where they differ; tokens by window totals over every actor.
decisions.why: Round 1 item 4 met: FR-010 names trees held AND the machine's load; the load band is now part of likeness and both loads are stated wherever they differ, as phase 5 repeats. FR-006 and FR-007 are carried by the token and task-size rows.

decisions.summary: make builder-tree refuses a handout while the clone holds unpushed commits, pointing at the DIRECT push; the moved waits=T<n> premise measured in phase 5, not built around.
decisions.why: Serves US1 ('nothing it writes waits on a gate') and FR-002's base.

decisions.summary: A successor or repair handout applies the earlier done commit without committing and supersedes its ref; a later hand-in waits while the earlier sits in an open batch.
decisions.why: Keeps closing halves from idling a tree under the lane; no requirement narrowed.

decisions.summary: Code layout: a new lane crate, the hand-in in the land crate, repairs in the shared queue.
decisions.why: Structure only.

decisions.summary: Six phases, each usable alone, with Verify lines; phase 5 measures over the first like window after phase 3.
decisions.why: Delivery order; the phase 2 and 3 Verify lines now reach the tripwire both ways, the integrate entry, and phase 5 applies D12's likeness test.

decisions.summary: The retirement table and the 451 parts taken over (T302 1 and 4, T307 1-3, T308's split, T405, T415), with T525 answered by D1.
decisions.why: Restates D1, D5, D10 and D11.

decisions.summary: Two writers of main (a second push failure filed as an integrate repair entry for a fresh builder), cost moved to builders judged by FR-006/FR-007, a wrong attribution, a wake that needs judgment.
decisions.why: Restates D7's routing; no new scope.

decisions.summary: The knob table (L7R_LANE_TREE, LANE_MAX, LANE_WAIT_S, LANE_RETRY, LANE_IDLE_S, HAND_IN_BASE, LANE_WAIT_MAX, LANE_REPAIR_FIRST, the trees-held band, LIKE_LOAD_BAND), each labeled.
decisions.why: Each knob belongs to a decision ruled above; labeled GUESS or the easier route.

decisions.summary: the lane's tree is the existing -land worktree, adopted into the pool under a reserved holder; T525's removal replaced
decisions.why: FR-003 asks for the lane's own worktree and leaves which one to the plan; nothing asked is dropped.

decisions.summary: a detached runner l7r-gate lane --work of the project's own, flock-held, restartable from its log
decisions.why: The sketch: 'run as a script in its own worktree rather than in my turns'; FR-009's reuse question is answered and priced.

decisions.summary: the hand-in's rebase is the builder's diff applied onto origin/main with the carry's rules (clone HEAD in phase 1), then the first pass, then the commit
decisions.why: FR-002's order kept literally; the no-rewrite rule forbids git rebase, and applying onto current main is what rebasing onto it delivers. Phase 1's base is where work lands while the coordinator still carries.

decisions.summary: the hand-in's first pass asks what the builder can answer; another writer's changes, the mark's hold, the tripwire and the gate's stamp rows are left to the lane's landing, asked there again
decisions.why: Asked literally in a builder's own tree, writer_refusal and the hold refuse for reasons no builder can cure, defeating the sketch's purpose ('bookkeeping refusals then get fixed by the builder that has the context'); every check left out is still asked at the lane's make land, so FR-008 loses nothing. No coverage runs, as FR-002 says.

decisions.summary: a batch starts at once on an idle lane; same-feature hand-ins in order up to LANE_MAX=6, GUESS knobs seeded from 458's absent finding
decisions.why: FR-004 makes size and start a knob seeded from 458; the seeding is stated and the order is FR-003's.

decisions.summary: red batch: attribute from the gate's record, else halve; eject; land the rest; tripwire keyed by task's second pin; the stand-down only for a run in the lane's tree with an open batch id or started by the lock-holding runner; a one-change red run pins why red
decisions.why: Round 2's two required changes are made: step 4 scopes second_red_gate's stand-down to a lane-tree run with a batch open in lane.jsonl or the lock holder's child, a by-hand make land with the variable meets the gate as today (phase 2's red-first fixtures, both ways), and an ejection after its own one-change red run pins why red. FR-004 and FR-008 literally.

decisions.summary: an ejected change becomes a repair entry in l7r-lane/repairs.jsonl a fresh builder takes; every integration wake's work goes to a fresh agent the coordinator dispatches
decisions.why: US4/US5 and the sketch: 'the ejected task returns to the queue as a repair entry'; the coordinator carries one line and one dispatch.

decisions.summary: computed states and one jsonl line a transition; each attempt its own file
decisions.why: Serves US4/FR-004's attribution and the night's lost causes; no behavior beyond the asked lane.

decisions.summary: make lane-wait in the background wakes the coordinator per batch and for US5's cases; a Stop rule keeps it armed
decisions.why: FR-005 literally; the Stop rule only enforces the asked wake-up. The knobs table's Stop-rule line now matches D9's body (round 2's aside).

decisions.summary: FR-001 by construction plus a two-tree guard fixture; T405 by option (C)
decisions.why: FR-001 taken over as the spec says; the fixture enforces it.

decisions.summary: T302 part 1 confirmed by reading; in phase 4 make land outside the lane refused (LAND_HERE_OK recorded), land-alone steps 1-6 retired, step 7 kept as take-tip.sh, writers.rs kept
decisions.why: The spec's takeover of T302 parts 1 and 4; FR-008's checks kept; the recorded escape covers only a broken lane.

decisions.summary: one measurement script over both windows; a like window by trees held within 0.5 and median load within 0.75-1.25 of the night's; tokens by actor over window totals
decisions.why: FR-006, FR-007 and FR-010 literally; the bands are labeled GUESS knobs and both concurrencies stated beside each figure.

decisions.summary: a handout refused while the clone holds unpushed commits, naming sync-with-main.sh done; the waits= wait measured in phase 5
decisions.why: Serves US1 ('nothing it writes waits on a gate') and D3's base; the premise it moves is measured, not built around.

decisions.summary: a successor builds on its earlier done commit by a no-commit apply and supersedes the ref; an open batch's shas fixed when it forms
decisions.why: Keeps trees from idling on a landing, the request's purpose; within FR-002/FR-003.

decisions.summary: a new lane crate and the hand-in in the land crate; file-scale plan

decisions.summary: five phases each usable alone, each with its Verify line; phase 2 adds the stand-down's red-first fixtures

decisions.summary: the 451 parts taken over and T525 answered
decisions.why: As the spec's takeover list names them.
